## Household and background

Theo Ramsey (born March 8, 1985 — 40) is single with no dependents and rents at 230 Juniper Lane in Anytown. He was an operations lead at Casella Distribution Warehouse until a spinal injury in late April took him off work: one W-2 for January through April (box 1 wages $17,942.00, box 2 withholding $1,435.00).

From May onward the company's long-term disability plan paid him $2,102.00 a month — $16,816.00 for the eight months, reported on a 1099-R with box 7 code 3. The premiums were entirely employer-paid, so the benefit is fully taxable (box 2a equals box 1). He did not set up withholding on the benefit and expects to owe a little. The plan's normal retirement age is 65, so at 40 he is far below the minimum retirement age — the benefit reports as wages on line 1h, not on the pension lines.

- 2025 Form W-2, Casella Distribution Warehouse (box 1 $17,942.00; box 2 $1,435.00 — January through April)

## Interview

**Q.** Have you reached the plan's minimum retirement age?

**A.** No — the plan's retirement age is 65 and I'm 40. The benefit is what the plan pays while I can't do my job.

**Q.** Who paid the disability-plan premiums — you or the company?

**A.** The company, entirely. I never paid anything after tax, so I understand the whole benefit is taxable.

**Q.** Are you permanently and totally disabled — unable to do any substantial work — as the IRS defines it?

**A.** No. My doctors expect me back at work next year; the plan covers me while I recover.

**Q.** Did you have any withholding taken from the benefit, or roll any of it over?

**A.** No withholding — I know I'll owe a bit at filing — and no, there was nothing to roll over.

**Q.** Any dependents? Could anyone claim you as a dependent? Are you blind or a student? A U.S. citizen all year?

**A.** No to all of those, and yes — citizen all year.

## Preparer notes

- Code 3 + NOT at minimum retirement age → the taxable disability benefit reports as WAGES on Form 1040 line 1h (Pub 575; i1040gi Line 1h bullet), never on lines 5a/5b.
- Fully taxable (employer-paid premiums) keeps the return on the narrow supported path: box 2a = box 1.
- Not 'permanently and totally disabled' for tax purposes (expected to return to work), so the filer-level disability flag stays No — the recovery story keeps the fact surface coherent.
- Total income $34,758; taxable income $19,008; withholding $1,435 only → a small balance due (no withholding was elected on the benefit).
